image_description: Two individuals standing outdoors in an academic setting. The person on the left wears a light gold/champagne colored academic gown and a mortarboard cap with a tassel. The person on the right wears a black academic gown with colorful velvet bars on the sleeves (indicating doctoral status) over a white shirt and tie. Both garments exhibit the characteristic wide, bell-shaped sleeves of academic regalia.

The black gown on the right clearly shows a center-front opening revealing the shirt/tie underneath. The gold gown on the left also follows this symmetrical open-front structure.
The fabric hangs loosely, hiding the specific shape of the torso and arms, consistent with the voluminous nature of academic robes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wide open sleeves extending well below hand level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The distinctive 'bell' or 'batwing' sleeves are clearly visible on both subjects, hanging significantly lower than the wrists/hands.
The front edges of the gowns form distinct panels that hang vertically, framing the wearer's chest.
The subject on the right is visibly wearing a collared shirt and tie. The subject on the left appears to be wearing formal clothing underneath the gown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Heavy matte fabric typically black polyester or wool blend.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The black gown exhibits a matte, heavy drape. The gold gown has a slight sheen but maintains the structural weight expected of ceremonial fabrics.
The fabric surfaces are smooth without complex patterns or excessive reflectivity, consistent with standard gown materials.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Characteristic sleeve drape extending past the wrist.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The sleeves flare outwards and downwards, extending well past the wrist line, which is the defining functional feature of this class.

The hands holding the object at the bottom center are somewhat indistinct and merge slightly with the gown folds and the object itself, lacking clear finger definition.

The presence of specific academic markers (mortarboard, velvet bars) reinforces the classification strongly.
